# Final Project

## Loading in the data
``` {r}
freq_data <- read.csv("data/freMTPL2freq.csv")
sev_data <- read.csv("data/freMTPL2sev.csv")
v_agg <- aggregate(ClaimAmount ~ IDpol, data = sev_data, FUN = sum)
total_data <- merge(freq_data, v_agg, by = "IDpol", all.x = TRUE)
total_data$ClaimAmount[is.na(total_data$ClaimAmount)] <- 0
count <- nrow(total_data)
```

## Summary Statistics
### ClaimNb
``` {r}
cat("The mean is ", mean( total_data$ClaimNb), "\n")
cat("The median is ", median(total_data$ClaimNb), "\n")
cat("The max is ", max(total_data$ClaimNb), "\n")
cat("The variance is ", var(total_data$ClaimNb), "\n")
num_zero_claims <- sum(total_data$ClaimNb == 0)
cat("The number of zero claims is", num_zero_claims, "\n")
percent_zero_claims <- num_zero_claims / count
cat("The percent of zero claims is ", percent_zero_claims, "\n")
```
Var > Mean suggesting overdispersion for Poisson models of ClaimNb

### Continuous Data
``` {r}
summarize_continuous <- function(df, var_name) {
  x <- df[[var_name]]
  
  cat("\n-----------", var_name, "-----------\n")
  cat("The mean is ", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("The median is ", median(x, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("The max is ", max(x, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("The variance is ", var(x, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  boxplot(x,
          main = paste("Distribution of", var_name),
          ylab = var_name,
          col = "lightblue")
  boxplot(log1p(x),
          main = paste("Log-Transformed:", var_name),
          ylab = paste0("log(", var_name, " + 1)"),
          col = "lightgreen")
  }
cont_vars <- c("DrivAge", "VehAge", "BonusMalus", "Density", "VehPower")

for (v in cont_vars) {
  summarize_continuous(total_data, v)
}
cat("\n BonusMalas min is", min(total_data$BonusMalus), "\n")
```
VehAge and Density seem to have very right skewed box plot which improve greatly after a log transformation. BonusMalus is right shewed in both the normal and log transformed box plots, Looking at a Swiss Actuarial Society paper(page 13) it seems that their approach to BonusMalus was to cap it at 150. 
``` {r}
total_data$VehAgeLog <- log(total_data$VehAge +1)
total_data$DensityLog <- log(total_data$Density + 1)
total_data$BonusMalusLimit <- pmin(total_data$BonusMalus, 150)
```
### Categorical Data
``` {r}
summarize_categorical <- function(df, var_name) {
  cat("\n-----------", var_name, "-----------\n")
  
  counts <- table(df[[var_name]])
  probs <- round(prop.table(counts) * 100, 2)
  mean_claims <- round(tapply(df$ClaimNb, df[[var_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
  mean_amount <- round(tapply(df$ClaimAmount, df[[var_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  
  summary_df <- data.frame(
    Level = names(counts),
    Count = as.numeric(counts),
    Percent = as.numeric(probs),
    Mean_ClaimNb = as.numeric(mean_claims),
    Mean_ClaimAmount = as.numeric(mean_amount)
  )
  
  print(summary_df, row.names = FALSE)
}
cat_vars <- c("Area", "VehBrand", "VehGas", "Region")

for (v in cat_vars) {
  summarize_categorical(total_data, v)
}
```
  Area is a categorical variable with highly rural areas being the first few letters such as A and B and highly urban areas as E, F being the last letter and the letters in between representing the inbetween those categories Area B has a much higher rate of claim amounts while most other areas are similar in that aspect. Claim rates seem to generally increase as the area gets more urban.

### General Analysis
``` {r}
pred_vars <- total_data[, c("DrivAge", "VehAgeLog", "BonusMalusLimit", "DensityLog", "VehPower", "Exposure")]

cat("\n------------ The correlation matrix is ------------\n")
corr_matrix <- cor(pred_vars, use = "complete.obs")
print(corr_matrix)
cat("\n------------ The correlation with ClaimAmount is ------------\n")
corr_claim_amount <- cor(pred_vars, total_data$ClaimAmount, use = "complete.obs")
print(corr_claim_amount)
cat("\n------------ The correlation with ClaimNb is ------------\n")
corr_claim_num <- cor(pred_vars, total_data$ClaimNb, use = "complete.obs")
print(corr_claim_num)
corrplot(corr_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper"
         )
corrplot(corr_claim_amount,
         method = "color"
         )
corrplot(corr_claim_num,
         method = "color"
         )
```
It seems that BonusMalus is moderately negatively correlated with DrivAge, other than that the risk of multicollinearity  seems quite low. However we should check the VIF scores
``` {r}
#creating model just to use the vif function
vif_model <- glm(
  ClaimNb ~ DrivAge + VehAgeLog + BonusMalusLimit + DensityLog + VehPower + Exposure + Area + VehBrand + VehGas + Region,
  data = total_data,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)
vif_results <- vif(vif_model)
print(vif_results)
```
There is extreme multicolinearity with Density and Area. This suggests that regularization methods may be effective.
## Model Creation

### Tweedie models
``` {r}
#It takes too long on the full dataset so we use a limited dataset for tweedie p selection
set.seed(123)
sub_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(total_data)), size = 25000)
sub_dataset <- total_data[sub_idx, ]
p_out <- tweedie_profile(
  ClaimAmount ~ DrivAge + VehAgeLog + BonusMalusLimit + DensityLog + VehPower + Exposure + VehBrand + VehGas + Region,
  data = sub_dataset,
  p.vec = seq(1.1, 1.9, by = 0.1),
  do.plot = TRUE
)
best_p <- p_out$p.max
```
